Valdis: Valdis has the occasionally annoying knack of systematising everything. It's drives his children batty, along with his long-suffering wife.
Van: Poker face. He has a very tight set of close friends and even they will tell you that Van is hard to crack into.
Vance: Vance dances like a robot in that he doesn't like getting has arms and hands too far from his body. It's all about keeping things in line, with Vance. He's a reserved kind of bloke and like most cats he'll relax once he gets familiar with  you.
Vander: For a name which sounds like it belongs on the side of an interplanetary rocket ship, Vander is a surprisingly mellow cat. Self-conscious, even. His friends can’t seem to do without him, and women move towards him as if empowered by some kind of subtle, lateral gravity. The whole career-thing is his only issue, mostly because decision making isn’t his best card. He’d much prefer to go with the proverbial flow.
Varian: Talk about white line fever. Varian steps off a plane at some foreign airport and it's like magic dust has been sprinkled over him. Sometimes he even changes his name. But all of it aims to rid him of the personality he is loaded with back home so he can explode out into the ether and become the quintissential, Masked Avenger!
Vasco: Vasco is a slick and super-smart Real Estate agent in either the Gold Coast or Miami. He wears a fat gold chain around his right wrist that matches the one around his neck, he drives a Mercedes convertible and he wouldn’t change his lot in life if you paid him, which is something that you wouldn’t have to do, anyway.
Vasilios: What is it about loud, laughing, demonstrative Greek men? After a while you just want them to leave, yet you can't help but watch and smile at the show. Vasilios.
Vass: Maurizio's business partner. They are famous in the nightclubs of Miami, the Gold Coast, Australia, and certain parts of Mexico City.
Vassilis: Vassilis retired when he hit 25. Sure, he plagiarised that first plot a little, because when there’s a corner to cut he’ll cut it. His theory is that in 100 years he’ll be dead so why will it matter?
Vaughan: Vaughan is six feet tall, wears big black sunglasses, a cheap suit (the trousers of which are four inches too short) and is a surprisingly good used-car salesman. He doesn’t like ripping off grannies but he can’t help it. They’re just too easy.
Vaughn: Vaughn, I know the spelling is different but that's okay. You and your kindred spirit arrive from the same egg so please check out Vaughan, above, and enjoy the ride.
Veejay: If you are happy and active you will always succeed - this is his mantra. If you’re going to hang out with Veejay there is an 80% probability that the rule book will be thrown out, and rightly so.
Vernon: You know the dream you have when you’re suddenly standing in a crowded restaurant or maybe in class, and you’re completely naked? Well, psycho-analysts in the 60’s coined that the Vernon Dream. I’ve no idea why.
Vic: The short name hides a complex individual. If Vic is bad he’s nasty but if he’s good he’s great. Whichever one he is, however, he prefers the outdoor life, usually, and he’s pretty good with most types of engines, and even though he sports a beer gut.
Victor: Victor is the name of a gold plated calligraphy pen that’s worth thousands, and who looks excellent when sticking out the top of a breast pocket.
Vigal: Vigal always looks kind of silly sitting in an office. He needs a cause to fire him up, you see. Plonk him in a cubicle and tell him he has to wear a tie and all the air will be sucked out of him immediately. It might even kill him.
Vince: Always has a form guide in his pocket and never sits down for longer than 7 minutes.
Vincent: All Vincents are ultra-sensitive souls who wrestle with their own substantial talents and personalities from the minute they draw first breathe. Often overcome with emotion, it’s no wonder Van Gough cut his own ear off and topped himself.
Virgil: Heralding from the same bloodline as Eugene and Herman, Virgil is anything but conventional. Yes, he is full of love and yes, he is a patient and compassionate man, but it's his playful ridiculousness that really warms the crowd. Ever seen the opening sequence of a television show called F-Troop, when Captain Palmenter is accidentally riding backwards on his horse? Well this kind of accidental but brilliantly conceived (by the gods) stunt is called A Virgil. Planet Earth therefore would be a much sadder place without him, and amen to that.
Vito: The subtle patriarch who doesn’t mind cutting corners, and who congratulates those who do when things turn out well. He’s never quite so agreeable if they don’t, however.
Vivian: What a perfectly humorous and gentle individual. True, there are one or two Vivians who, due to their surroundings, have needed to become incredibly tough and dangerous, but let me tell you these specimens are rarely spotted in the wild. Your stock-standard Vivian is rarely short, he is a reader, he is a thinker, and he has odd, albeit, harmless hobbies - like collecting teaspoons for instance. It all just adds another part of the puzzle that IS Vivian.
Vlad:
Vlad is the kind of man who will insist he's a really funny guy while he's got a revolver aimed at the middle of your forehead. 
“Yeah, Vlad, you’re fuckin’ hilarious mate,” is the general response.
Von: Authentic and eager without being effusive, Von is skilled at devising a framework around a problem or a situation and then seeing it executed. And he has a wicked sense of humour (when he’s not working).
Vosso: Vosso always struggles in business because he does more than what he says he's going to do. I know, we didn't anticipate that either up here in the commentary box. Vosso, a word of advice: give from a position of power, not from a position of weakness. That way you benefit as well.
Vossy: Fairy floss, my arse. Vossy is a competitor and don't let the comfy sounding name give you the wrong impression. The heat of battle is where he does his best work.
